Natural_Language: This part prescribes (a) the basic requirements of contracting for supplies and services (including construction) by sealed bidding, (b) the information to be included in the invitation for bids (IFB), (c) procedures concerning the submission of bids, (d) requirements for opening, evaluating bids, awarding contracts, and (e) procedures for two-step sealed bidding.
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_000_a: Part 14 prescribes basic requirements of contracting by sealed bidding; P_14_000_b: Part 14 prescribes information to be included in IFB; P_14_000_c: Part 14 prescribes procedures concerning submission of bids; P_14_000_d: Part 14 prescribes requirements for opening, evaluating bids, and awarding contracts; P_14_000_e: Part 14 prescribes procedures for two-step sealed bidding
Validation_Notes: Scope statement establishing five conjunctive areas covered by Part 14. All five are descriptive of part coverage, not prescriptive requirements. Straightforward conjunction.

Natural_Language: General requirements for sealed bidding (Subpart 14.1).
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_1: General requirements for sealed bidding consist of paragraphs (a), (b), and (c)
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for Subpart 14.1. Three subsections are conjunctively required.

Natural_Language: Sealed bidding is a method of contracting that employs competitive bids, public opening of bids, and awards.
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_1_a_1: Sealed bidding employs competitive bids; P_14_1_a_2: Sealed bidding employs public opening of bids; P_14_1_a_3: Sealed bidding employs awards
Validation_Notes: Definitional statement. Three elements define sealed bidding. All three are necessary characteristics. Declarative 'is' establishes definition rather than mandate.

Natural_Language: Use sealed bidding whenever the conditions in 6.101(b) are met.
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_1_b_a: Conditions in 6.101(b) are met; P_14_1_b_b: Sealed bidding is used
Validation_Notes: Mandatory conditional: meeting conditions in 6.101(b) triggers requirement to use sealed bidding. 'Whenever' indicates material implication. External dependency on Part 6. HIGH-RISK because implication could be read as biconditional (sealed bidding used ONLY when conditions met), but text does not say 'only when.'

Natural_Language: The contracting officer must use firm-fixed-price contracts when using sealed bidding or fixed-price contracts with economic price adjustment clauses when some flexibility is necessary and feasible.
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_1_c_a: Sealed bidding is being used; P_14_1_c_b: CO uses firm-fixed-price contracts; P_14_1_c_c: Some flexibility is necessary and feasible; P_14_1_c_d: CO uses fixed-price contracts with economic price adjustment clauses
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Two conditional paths: default is FFP when using sealed bidding; FP-EPA permitted when flexibility necessary and feasible. 'Must' makes both paths mandatory under their respective conditions. The 'or' here is exclusive based on whether flexibility condition is met. HIGH-RISK because the two implications partition the sealed bidding condition.

Natural_Language: Preparation of invitations for bids.
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_201: Preparation of invitations for bids encompasses format, uniform contract format, requirements, economic purchase quantities, bid samples, descriptive literature, and solicitation provisions
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for Subpart 14.2 Presolicitation. All subsections are conjunctively required components of IFB preparation.

Natural_Language: Format requirements for IFBs.
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_201_1: Format requirements encompass uniform contract format use, exceptions, and simplified contract format option
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for section 14.201-1 format requirements.

Natural_Language: Contracting officers must prepare invitation for bids and contracts using parts I, II, III, and IV of the uniform contract format (see part 15) to the maximum practicable extent.
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_201_1_a_a: COs prepare IFBs and contracts using uniform contract format parts I-IV; P_14_201_1_a_b: Use is to maximum practicable extent
Validation_Notes: Mandatory requirement ('must') qualified by 'to the maximum practicable extent.' Conjunction of the action and its qualifier. External reference to Part 15.

Natural_Language: The uniform contract format is not required when contracting for: (1) Construction (see part 36); (2) Shipbuilding (including design, construction, and conversion), ship overhaul, and ship repair; (3) Subsistence items; (4) Supplies or services requiring special contract forms prescribed elsewhere in this regulation that are inconsistent with the uniform contract format; or (5) Firm-fixed-price or fixed-price with economic price adjustment acquisitions that use the simplified contract format.
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_201_1_b_1: Contracting for construction; P_14_201_1_b_2: Contracting for shipbuilding, ship overhaul, or ship repair; P_14_201_1_b_3: Contracting for subsistence items; P_14_201_1_b_4: Supplies or services requiring special contract forms inconsistent with UCF; P_14_201_1_b_5: FFP or FP-EPA acquisitions using simplified contract format; P_14_201_1_b_x: Uniform contract format is not required
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Disjunction (Add): Rule 8; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Any one of five disjunctive conditions triggers exception to UCF requirement. 'Or' at end of list confirms disjunction. Each exception independently sufficient. Negates the parent requirement in P_14_201_1_a. HIGH-RISK: implication used to model exception to general rule.

Natural_Language: The contracting officer may use the simplified contract format in lieu of the uniform contract format.
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_201_1_c_1_a: CO uses simplified contract format in lieu of uniform contract format
Validation_Notes: Permissive 'may' creates discretionary authority. Tautology represents unrestricted choice. CO has full discretion to use or not use simplified format.

Natural_Language: The contracting officer has flexibility in preparation and organization of the simplified contract format.
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_201_1_c_2: CO has flexibility in simplified contract format preparation and organization
Validation_Notes: Parent for simplified contract format elements. 'Should be used to the maximum extent practical' is advisory, not mandatory. PENDING_REVIEW due to advisory 'should.'

Natural_Language: Use Standard Form (SF) 1447, Solicitation/Contract, as the first page of the IFB.
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_201_1_c_2_i_a: SF 1447 is used as first page of IFB
Validation_Notes: Advisory requirement under 'should' framework of parent. Single atomic proposition. Format is advisory per parent's 'should' qualifier.

Natural_Language: Include the following for each line item: (A) Line item number. (B) Description of supplies or services, or data sufficient to identify the requirement. (C) Quantity and unit of issue. (D) Unit price and amount. (E) Packaging and marking requirements. (F) Inspection and acceptance, quality assurance, and reliability requirements. (G) Place of delivery, performance and delivery dates, period of performance, and f.o.b. point. (H) Other item-peculiar information as necessary (e.g., individual fund citations).
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_201_1_c_2_ii_A: Line item number included; P_14_201_1_c_2_ii_B: Description of supplies or services included; P_14_201_1_c_2_ii_C: Quantity and unit of issue included; P_14_201_1_c_2_ii_D: Unit price and amount included; P_14_201_1_c_2_ii_E: Packaging and marking requirements included; P_14_201_1_c_2_ii_F: Inspection and acceptance, quality assurance, and reliability requirements included; P_14_201_1_c_2_ii_G: Place of delivery, performance and delivery dates, period of performance, and f.o.b. point included; P_14_201_1_c_2_ii_H: Other item-peculiar information as necessary included
Validation_Notes: Eight conjunctive line item elements under advisory 'should' framework. All eight required for each line item when using simplified format. Item (H) includes discretionary 'as necessary' qualifier. PENDING_REVIEW due to parent advisory status.

Natural_Language: Include the clauses required by this regulation. Additional clauses must be incorporated only when necessary to the particular acquisition.
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_201_1_c_2_iii_a: Required clauses included; P_14_201_1_c_2_iii_b: Additional clauses incorporated only when necessary to particular acquisition
Validation_Notes: Two-part requirement: mandatory inclusion of required clauses, and conditional limitation on additional clauses. 'Must' in second sentence is mandatory. HIGH-RISK for implication modeling the necessity condition.

Natural_Language: List of documents and attachments (include if necessary).
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_201_1_c_2_iv_a: Necessity for documents and attachments list exists; P_14_201_1_c_2_iv_b: List of documents and attachments included
Validation_Notes: Conditional inclusion: 'if necessary' triggers inclusion. Advisory under parent 'should' framework. HIGH-RISK: conditional trigger on necessity determination.

Natural_Language: Representations and instructions: (A) Insert the IFB provisions that require representations, certifications, or the submission of other information by offerors. (B) Insert the IFB provisions required by 14.207. Include any other information/instructions necessary to guide offerors. (C) Insert all price related evaluation factors and any significant price related subfactors for award. (D) Upon award, the contracting officer must retain the representations and instructions in the contract file.
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_201_1_c_2_v_A: IFB provisions requiring representations, certifications, or other information inserted; P_14_201_1_c_2_v_B: IFB provisions required by 14.207 and other necessary information/instructions inserted; P_14_201_1_c_2_v_C: All price related evaluation factors and significant subfactors inserted; P_14_201_1_c_2_v_D: Upon award, CO retains representations and instructions in contract file
Validation_Notes: Four conjunctive requirements for representations and instructions section. Item (D) uses mandatory 'must' for post-award retention. Items (A)-(C) are advisory under parent 'should' but item (D) is independently mandatory. PENDING_REVIEW due to mixed advisory/mandatory elements.

Natural_Language: Uniform contract format.
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_202: Uniform contract format encompasses Part I Schedule, Part II Contract clauses, Part III Documents/exhibits/attachments, and Part IV Representations and instructions
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for section 14.202. Four parts of uniform contract format are conjunctively required.

Natural_Language: The contracting officer must prepare the Schedule as follows.
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_202_1: Part I Schedule preparation encompasses Sections A through H
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. 'Must prepare' makes all sections mandatory. Eight conjunctive sections (A-H) required.

Natural_Language: Section A, Solicitation/contract form.
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_202_1_a: Section A requirements include standard form selection and required content if standard forms not used
Validation_Notes: Parent for Section A. Two conjunctive subsections covering form selection and alternative content requirements.

Natural_Language: For sealed bidding the SF 33 or the SF 1447 may be used. When the SF 1447 is used as the IFB document, insert the information in subdivisions (a)(2)(i) and (a)(2)(iv) of this section in block 9 of the SF 1447.
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_202_1_a_1_a: SF 33 is used for sealed bidding; P_14_202_1_a_1_b: SF 1447 is used for sealed bidding; P_14_202_1_a_1_c: SF 1447 is used as IFB document; P_14_202_1_a_1_d: Information from (a)(2)(i) and (a)(2)(iv) inserted in block 9 of SF 1447
Justification_Rules: Disjunction (Add): Rule 8; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]
Validation_Notes: Permissive 'may' for form selection (disjunction). Conditional requirement when SF 1447 used as IFB. HIGH-RISK: implication models the 'when' conditional for SF 1447 usage.

Natural_Language: If the SF 33 or the SF 1447 are not used, include the following on the first page of the invitation for bids: (i) Name, address, and location of issuing activity, including room and building where bids must be submitted. (ii) Invitation for bids number. (iii) Date of issuance. (iv) Time specified for receipt of bids. (v) Number of pages. (vi) Requisition or other purchase authority. (vii) Requirement for a bidder to provide its name and complete address, including street, city, county, State, and ZIP code. (viii) A statement that bidders should include in the bid the address to which payment should be mailed, if that address is different from that of the bidder.
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_202_1_a_2_cond: SF 33 and SF 1447 are not used; P_14_202_1_a_2_i: Name, address, and location of issuing activity included; P_14_202_1_a_2_ii: IFB number included; P_14_202_1_a_2_iii: Date of issuance included; P_14_202_1_a_2_iv: Time specified for receipt of bids included; P_14_202_1_a_2_v: Number of pages included; P_14_202_1_a_2_vi: Requisition or other purchase authority included; P_14_202_1_a_2_vii: Requirement for bidder name and complete address included; P_14_202_1_a_2_viii: Statement about payment mailing address included
Validation_Notes: Conditional trigger: not using standard forms requires eight conjunctive elements on first page. Item (viii) uses advisory 'should' but is framed as a required statement to be included, making its inclusion mandatory even though the bidder action it describes is advisory. HIGH-RISK: implication on negative condition.

Natural_Language: Section B, Supplies or services and prices. (1) See 15.108-1(b). (2) Optional Form 336 (OF 336), Continuation Sheet, may be used.
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_202_1_b_1: Section B content per 15.108-1(b); P_14_202_1_b_2: OF 336 may be used
Validation_Notes: Mandatory reference to Part 15 for Section B content. OF 336 use is permissive ('may'). Tautology for permissive element.

Natural_Language: Section C, Description/specifications (see 15.108-1(c)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_202_1_c_a: Section C prepared per 15.108-1(c)
Validation_Notes: Direct cross-reference to Part 15 for Section C content. Single atomic requirement.

Natural_Language: Section D, Packaging and marking (see 15.108-1(d)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_202_1_d_a: Section D prepared per 15.108-1(d)
Validation_Notes: Direct cross-reference to Part 15 for Section D.

Natural_Language: Section E, Inspection and acceptance (see 15.108-1(e)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_202_1_e_a: Section E prepared per 15.108-1(e)
Validation_Notes: Direct cross-reference to Part 15 for Section E.

Natural_Language: Section F, Deliveries or performance (see 15.108-1(f)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_202_1_f_a: Section F prepared per 15.108-1(f)
Validation_Notes: Direct cross-reference to Part 15 for Section F.

Natural_Language: Section G, Contract administration data (see 15.108-1(g)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_202_1_g_a: Section G prepared per 15.108-1(g)
Validation_Notes: Direct cross-reference to Part 15 for Section G.

Natural_Language: Section H, Special contract requirements (see 15.108-1(h)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_202_1_h_a: Section H prepared per 15.108-1(h)
Validation_Notes: Direct cross-reference to Part 15 for Section H.

Natural_Language: Section I, Contract clauses (see 15.108-2).
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_202_2_a: Section I prepared per 15.108-2
Validation_Notes: Direct cross-reference to Part 15 for Section I.

Natural_Language: Section J, List of documents, exhibits, and other attachments (see 15.108-3).
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_202_3_a: Section J prepared per 15.108-3
Validation_Notes: Direct cross-reference to Part 15 for Section J.

Natural_Language: The contracting officer must prepare the representations and instructions as follows.
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_202_4: Part IV encompasses Sections K, L, and M
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. 'Must prepare' makes all three sections mandatory.

Natural_Language: Section K, Representations, certifications, and other statements of bidders (see 15.108-4(a)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_202_4_a_1: Section K prepared per 15.108-4(a)
Validation_Notes: Direct cross-reference to Part 15 for Section K.

Natural_Language: Section L, Instructions, conditions, and notices to bidders (see 15.108-4(b)). The contracting officer must include the time and place for bid openings.
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_202_4_b_1: Section L prepared per 15.108-4(b); P_14_202_4_b_2: CO includes time and place for bid openings
Validation_Notes: Two conjunctive requirements: Part 15 cross-reference and mandatory inclusion of bid opening time/place. 'Must' makes both mandatory.

Natural_Language: Section M, Evaluation factors for award (see 15.108-4(c)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_202_4_c_1: Section M prepared per 15.108-4(c)
Validation_Notes: Direct cross-reference to Part 15 for Section M.

Natural_Language: IFB Requirements.
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_203: IFB requirements encompass description, prohibition on restrictive specs, inclusion of documents, evaluation statement, and qualification requirements
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for section 14.203. Five conjunctive requirements for IFB content.

Natural_Language: An IFB must clearly, accurately, and completely describe the Government requirements.
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_203_a_1: IFB describes Government requirements clearly; P_14_203_a_2: IFB describes Government requirements accurately; P_14_203_a_3: IFB describes Government requirements completely
Validation_Notes: Three conjunctive quality standards for IFB description. 'Must' makes all three mandatory. Clear, accurate, and complete are independent criteria.

Natural_Language: Restrictive specifications or requirements that might unduly limit the number of bidders are prohibited.
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_203_b_a: Specifications or requirements are restrictive and might unduly limit bidders; P_14_203_b_b: Such specifications or requirements are prohibited
Validation_Notes: Prohibition modeled as: if restrictive and unduly limiting, then prohibited (negation of their use). 'Might unduly limit' introduces subjective threshold. HIGH-RISK: implication on prohibition with subjective trigger condition.

Natural_Language: Include all documents and information (whether attached or incorporated by reference) prospective bidders will need for the purpose of bidding.
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_203_c_a: All documents and information needed for bidding are included (attached or by reference)
Validation_Notes: Mandatory inclusion requirement. Single atomic. 'Will need' establishes the scope of what must be included.

Natural_Language: The contracting officer must state in the invitation for bids that bids will be evaluated without discussions (see 52.214-10 and, for construction contracts, 52.214-19).
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_203_d_a: IFB states bids will be evaluated without discussions
Validation_Notes: Mandatory statement requirement. 'Must state' is unambiguous mandate. External references to FAR clauses 52.214-10 and 52.214-19.

Natural_Language: When considering establishing qualification requirements, see and follow subpart 9.2.
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_203_e_a: CO is considering establishing qualification requirements; P_14_203_e_b: CO follows subpart 9.2
Validation_Notes: Conditional: considering qualification requirements triggers requirement to follow subpart 9.2. 'When' functions as conditional trigger. HIGH-RISK: implication on a subjective precondition ('considering').

Natural_Language: Contracting officers must comply with the economic purchase quantity planning requirements for supplies in part 7. See part 7 for instructions regarding use of the provision at 52.207-4, Economic Purchase Quantity-Supplies, and for guidance on handling responses to that provision.
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_204_a: COs comply with economic purchase quantity planning requirements in part 7
Validation_Notes: Mandatory compliance requirement. 'Must comply' is unambiguous. External reference to Part 7 and clause 52.207-4. Second sentence is informational cross-reference, not separate requirement.

Natural_Language: Bid samples.
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_205: Bid samples requirements encompass conditions for requiring, IFB statements, waivers, unrequired samples, and return procedures
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for section 14.205. Six conjunctive subsections.

Natural_Language: The contracting officer must not require bidders to furnish bid samples unless: (1) Characteristics of the product cannot be described adequately in the specification or purchase description; (2) Necessary to determine the responsiveness of the bid. Do not use samples to determine a bidder's ability to produce the required items; and (3) Products must be suitable from the standpoint of balance, facility of use, general feel, color, pattern, or other characteristics that cannot be described adequately in the specification.
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_205_a_0: CO requires bid samples; P_14_205_a_1: Product characteristics cannot be described adequately in specification; P_14_205_a_2: Samples necessary to determine bid responsiveness (not bidder ability); P_14_205_a_3: Products must be suitable from standpoint of characteristics that cannot be described adequately
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Prohibition with three conjunctive exceptions. 'Must not...unless' creates negative default with conditional override. All three conditions must be met simultaneously ('and' connector) for bid samples to be permissible. Includes internal prohibition against using samples for bidder ability assessment. HIGH-RISK: complex negated implication with conjunctive exceptions.

Natural_Language: If the contracting officer requires bid samples, the IFB must state: (1) The number and, if appropriate, size, and description of the bid samples required; and (2) List all the characteristics for which the bid samples will be examined.
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_205_b_cond: CO requires bid samples; P_14_205_b_1: IFB states number, size, and description of samples required; P_14_205_b_2: IFB lists all characteristics for which samples will be examined
Validation_Notes: Conditional: requiring bid samples triggers two mandatory IFB content requirements. Both required conjunctively. HIGH-RISK: implication on conditional trigger.

Natural_Language: Contracting officers may waive bid sample requirements when a bidder offers a product previously or currently contracted for or tested by the Government and found to comply with specification requirements conforming in every material respect with those in the current invitation for bids. (See 14.207(j)(2)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_205_c_1_a: Bidder offers product previously/currently contracted for or tested by Government; P_14_205_c_1_b: Product found to comply with spec requirements conforming in every material respect; P_14_205_c_1_c: CO waives bid sample requirements
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: Permissive 'may' creates discretionary waiver. Two conjunctive conditions create eligibility. Tautology represents CO discretion.

Natural_Language: Where samples required by a Federal, Military, or other formal specification are not considered necessary and a waiver of the sample requirements of the specification is authorized, include a statement in the invitation that notwithstanding the requirements of the specification, samples are not required.
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_205_c_2_a: Spec-required samples not considered necessary; P_14_205_c_2_b: Waiver of spec sample requirements authorized; P_14_205_c_2_c: IFB includes statement that samples not required
Validation_Notes: Conditional: two conjunctive conditions trigger mandatory IFB statement.

Natural_Language: Bid samples furnished with a bid that are not required by the invitation generally will not be considered as qualifying the bid and will be disregarded. However, the bid sample will not be disregarded if it is clear from the bid or accompanying papers that the bidder's intention was to qualify the bid. If the qualification does not conform to the IFB, see 14.306-3(d).
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_205_d_a: Samples furnished but not required; P_14_205_d_b: Samples disregarded; P_14_205_d_c: Clear bidder intended to qualify bid; P_14_205_d_d: Sample not disregarded; P_14_205_d_e: Qualification does not conform to IFB; P_14_205_d_f: Process per 14.306-3(d)
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Three conditional paths: default disregard; exception for clear intent; sub-exception for nonconforming qualification. Multiple sequential implications.

Natural_Language: Return of bid samples: (1) Return samples not destroyed in testing to bidders at their request and expense, unless otherwise specified. (2) Request disposition instructions from bidders. (3) Return collect if disposition instructions not received within 30 days. Small items by prepaid mail. (4) Transmit inspection samples to inspecting activity with retention instructions. (5) Dispose consumed or impaired samples as scrap unless bidder requests return.
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_205_e_1: Non-destroyed samples returned at bidder request/expense unless invitation specifies otherwise; P_14_205_e_2: Disposition instructions requested; P_14_205_e_3: Return collect within 30 days if no instructions; P_14_205_e_4: Inspection samples transmitted to inspecting activity; P_14_205_e_5: Consumed/impaired samples disposed as scrap unless bidder requests return
Validation_Notes: Five conjunctive procedural requirements for sample return. Each independently enforceable.

Natural_Language: Descriptive literature.
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_206: Descriptive literature requirements encompass conditions for requiring, documentation, IFB statements, waivers, and unrequired literature procedures
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for section 14.206.

Natural_Language: Contracting officers must not require bidders to furnish descriptive literature unless it is needed before award to determine whether the products offered meet the specification and to establish exactly what the bidder proposes to furnish.
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_206_a_cond: Descriptive literature needed before award to determine product compliance and establish what bidder proposes; P_14_206_a_req: CO requires descriptive literature
Validation_Notes: Prohibition with exception: 'must not...unless' creates default prohibition. Two conjunctive purposes must be met for exception.

Natural_Language: The contracting officer must document in the contract file the justification why product acceptability cannot be determined without the submission of descriptive literature, except when the contract specifications require submission.
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_206_b_a: CO documents justification in contract file; P_14_206_b_b: Contract specifications require submission
Validation_Notes: Mandatory documentation with exception. When specs require submission, justification excused.

Natural_Language: If the invitation will require descriptive literature, the IFB must clearly state: (i) What descriptive literature the bidders must furnish; (ii) The purpose for requiring the literature; (iii) The extent of its consideration in the evaluation of bids; and (iv) The rules that will apply if a bidder fails to furnish the literature before bid opening or if the literature provided does not comply.
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_206_c_1_cond: Invitation requires descriptive literature; P_14_206_c_1_i: IFB states what literature required; P_14_206_c_1_ii: IFB states purpose; P_14_206_c_1_iii: IFB states extent of consideration; P_14_206_c_1_iv: IFB states rules for failure/noncompliance
Validation_Notes: Conditional: requiring literature triggers four mandatory IFB content elements.

Natural_Language: If bidders must furnish descriptive literature, see 14.207(k).
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_206_c_2_a: Bidders must furnish descriptive literature; P_14_206_c_2_b: Follow 14.207(k)
Validation_Notes: Simple conditional cross-reference.

Natural_Language: The contracting officer may waive the requirement for descriptive literature if: (i) The bidder states in the bid that the product being offered is the same as a product previously or currently being furnished to the contracting activity; and (ii) The contracting officer determines that the product offered complies with the specification requirements of the current invitation for bids. When the contracting officer waives the requirement, see 14.207(k)(2).
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_206_d_1_i: Bidder states product same as previously/currently furnished; P_14_206_d_1_ii: CO determines product complies with current spec requirements; P_14_206_d_1_w: CO waives literature requirement
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: Permissive 'may' with two conjunctive conditions. Tautology for discretion.

Natural_Language: When descriptive literature is not necessary and a waiver of literature requirements of a specification has been authorized, the contracting officer must include a statement in the invitation that, despite the requirements of the specifications, descriptive literature is not required.
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_206_d_2_a: Literature not necessary; P_14_206_d_2_b: Waiver authorized; P_14_206_d_2_c: CO includes statement in invitation
Validation_Notes: Conditional: two conditions trigger mandatory IFB statement.

Natural_Language: If the IFB provides for a waiver, a bidder may submit a bid on the basis of either the descriptive literature furnished with the bid or a previously furnished product. If the bid is submitted on one basis, the bidder may not have it considered on the other basis after bids are opened.
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_206_d_3_cond: IFB provides for waiver; P_14_206_d_3_a: Submit on basis of literature; P_14_206_d_3_b: Submit on basis of previously furnished product; P_14_206_d_3_c: Cannot switch basis after opening
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Disjunction (Add): Rule 8; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7
Validation_Notes: Conditional with exclusive choice and post-opening lock. Functionally exclusive disjunction due to prohibition on switching.

Natural_Language: If descriptive literature is furnished when it is not required by the invitation for bids, follow the procedures at 14.205(d).
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_206_e_cond: Literature furnished when not required; P_14_206_e_act: Follow 14.205(d)
Validation_Notes: Simple conditional cross-reference.

Natural_Language: Solicitation Provisions.
Atomic_Propositions: P_14_207: Solicitation provisions encompass general applicability and specific clause insertion requirements (a) through (q)
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for section 14.207.

Natural_Language: The provisions prescribed in this section apply to preparation and submission of bids in general. See other FAR parts for provisions and clauses related to specific acquisition requirements.

Natural_Language: Two-step sealed bidding is a combination of competitive procedures designed to obtain the benefits of sealed bidding when adequate specifications are not available. An objective is to permit the development of a sufficiently descriptive and not unduly restrictive statement of the Government's requirements, including an adequate technical data package, so that subsequent acquisitions may use conventional sealed bidding methods.

Natural_Language: Step one consists of the request for submission of technical proposals, evaluation, and (if necessary) discussion of a technical proposal. No pricing is submitted with step one. The objective is to determine the acceptability of the supplies or services offered. Conformity to the technical requirements is resolved in this step, but not responsibility as defined in part 9.

Validation_Notes: Five conjunctive definitional elements of step one. Item 2 is a prohibition (no pricing). Item 5 explicitly excludes responsibility determination. All descriptive.

Natural_Language: Step two involves the submission of sealed priced bids by those who submitted acceptable technical proposals in step one. Bids submitted in step two are evaluated and the awards made in accordance with subpart 14.3.

Validation_Notes: Two conjunctive definitional elements of step two. Participation limited to step one acceptees. Evaluation per standard sealed bidding rules.

Natural_Language: Unless other factors require the use of sealed bidding, the contracting officer may use two-step sealed bidding rather than negotiation when all of the following conditions are present: (1) Available specifications or purchase descriptions are not definite or complete or may be too restrictive without technical evaluation; (2) Definite criteria exist for evaluating technical proposals; (3) More than one technically qualified source is expected to be available; (4) There is sufficient time to use the two-step method; (5) The CO intends to award a firm-fixed-price contract or a fixed-price contract with economic price adjustment.

Natural_Language: None of the following precludes the use of two-step sealed bidding: (1) Multi-year contracting; (2) Government property to be made available to the successful bidder; (3) A total small business set-aside; (4) HUBZone set-aside or price evaluation preference; (5) SDVOSB set-aside; (6) EDWOSB/WOSB set-aside; (7) A first or subsequent production quantity under a performance specification.
